candidates.prompt: An acorn woodpecker (Melanerpes formicivorus), single adult male perched upright, side-on neutral pose, as if gripping a vertical trunk but no tree modelled. Realistic proportions, 21 cm long, compact body, short neck, straight chisel bill as long as the head. Clown face: black mask around bill and eye, white forehead band continuing down in front of the eye into a pale yellow throat, bright red crown, pale cream iris. Glossy blue-black back, wings and stiff pointed tail; black breast band streaking into a white belly; white rump. Wings folded. Zygodactyl feet, two toes forward, two back. No base, no branch. Game-ready, symmetric.

candidates.review: Upright perched bird with folded wings and a long tail hanging down, but it reads as a generic crested woodpecker, as the brief predicted: a spiky sawtooth crest on the crown and nape (an acorn woodpecker has a smooth rounded crown), a thin needle bill rather than a stout chisel, a slim elongated body rather than a compact one, a long tail with a forked tip rather than stiff pointed central feathers. Despite "no branch" it stands on a fused vertical stub (the lower fifth of the model) that the toes grip, so zygodactyl toes cannot be checked. Eye is a raised bump. Topology: one watertight piece (post included), 0 open edges, 0.9% slivers; 1.9 units tall, +y up, bill toward +z. Build script would have to cut the stub below the toes and rebuild zygodactyl feet, flatten the crest, replace the bill with a chisel cone, shorten and stiffen the tail, and paint the clown face by landmark regions: little of the generated geometry beyond the body and folded-wing mass survives.

accuracy_notes: Nothing adopted. The species is told by its clown face (black mask, white forehead band into a pale yellow throat, red cap, pale iris), the female's black band between forehead and cap, a white rump and white primary patch in flight, and a compact body braced on a stiff tail on granary trunks. The first Meshy candidate has the wrong head (crest, needle bill) and a fused perch; the face is painted from the palette in any case.
